comments.text:
Belgium: The Country Where Surrealism Never Left
Here, you can drink beer older than some nations, eat fries that are officially not French, and debate—in three languages—who makes the best mayonnaise. René Magritte knew it all along. He wasn’t painting surrealism; he was painting Belgium. A man in a bowler hat standing behind an apple? That’s just someone waiting for the train. A pipe with the words “Ceci n’est pas une pipe”? That’s Belgian logic: nothing is ever quite what it seems.
In Belgium, you can live in Flanders, work in Brussels, have family in Wallonia, and still spend hours arguing over the correct name for a pastry. There are six governments, hundreds of beers, and an endless supply of compromises. Strangely enough… it works ( for a while)
And above all :  René Magritte did grasp the logic!!!
